d4m3-a1.title: Section Audit — the Mediation Binder as drafted
d4m3-a1.kicker: Audit all six sections before Atty. Thorne approves delivery.
d4m3-a1.intro: The Litigation Desk assembled the binder on 03/02/2027 from the providers' original bills, and Atty. Grant Mercer says Keystone will not put a real number on the table while the medical ledger is unverified. On this draft he is right. Work the six sections.

items.as: Parties, counsel and the session date; start time and location "to be confirmed"; mediator's fee "split 50/50 (assumed)".
items.issue: On the morning of 03/18/2027 nobody can tell from the binder where to be or when. And a fee split the firm never agreed to is a bill it did not expect: the order says how the mediator is paid.
items.fix: Take the start time, location and the carrier's video link from the mediator's confirmation and the fee split from the mediation order; verify every contact and date it.

items.as: Draft 1, eight pages, in the binder; not yet routed to Atty. Thorne.
items.issue: It is our own position and our own concessions, for the mediator alone. A draft of it going out, or going out unapproved, is not the Case Manager's call to make either way.
items.fix: Route it to Atty. Thorne for approval, mark every page for the mediator only, keep it to one copy, and calendar its delivery with the binder.

items.as: The pre-filing draft: unsigned, no case number, the Property Damage counts missing.
items.issue: A superseded draft is not the operative pleading, and it leaves out counts that are actually in suit. In front of the mediator it invites an argument about what was pleaded at all.
items.fix: Replace it with the Complaint filed 09/24/2026, No. 26-CV-04417, and take the draft out of the binder set entirely.

items.as: The served copy, with the Complaint, as exhibits M-3 and M-4.
items.issue: The operative answer is what the mediator needs: it is the list of everything the other side intends to argue, and this file can answer all of it.
items.fix: Confirm it is the served copy, and that every allegation in it appears in the defense map below.

items.as: Not in the set. The pleaded allegations sit in the answer with nothing opposite them.
items.issue: Every allegation in the answer is already answerable from documents on this file. Without the map the mediator hears each one answered by a sentence instead of a page, and Atty. Thorne has to find the exhibit himself.
items.fix: Add the map: each pleaded allegation against the exhibit that answers it, by exhibit number. Flag the two legal questions for Atty. Thorne rather than answering them.

items.what: Police Report RPD-26-018842 and Ruth Calloway's statement
items.as: Exhibits M-5 and M-6, the certified report and the signed scene statement.
items.issue: The citation and an independent witness who signed at the scene: the answer to the out-of-turn allegation, in the operative copies.
items.fix: Confirm the report is the certified copy and the witness signature and date are legible, and seat both against the out-of-turn allegation in the defense map.

items.as: Filed with the liability exhibits; the stills on this file are the grayscale export of the 02/19/2026 working copy.
items.issue: The clearest liability proof on the file, and in grayscale the stop line is hard to read. An exhibit the mediator cannot see is an exhibit that argues nothing.
items.fix: Re-export the stills in color from the native file, hash unchanged, and enclose the preservation and chain-of-custody log with them.

items.as: The carrier's letters, February to April 2026, as exhibits M-7 to M-9.
items.issue: Among them is Keystone's acceptance of Property Damage liability on 02/17/2026, and the rental cutoff that begins the April disruption. Both are the carrier's own writing.
items.fix: Confirm the 02/17/2026 letter and the rental cutoff are in the set; what weight the liability acceptance carries is Atty. Thorne's call, not the binder's.

items.as: The desk note says the transcript is received and the summary is not yet added.
items.issue: The one record of what John Doe said under oath about the gap, the April break, the 2021 visits and the seatbelt, and it is not in the room.
items.fix: Add a summary with the certified transcript pages on each of those four points, marked in the index so Atty. Thorne can reach any of them in seconds.

items.as: Assembled from the providers' original bills: Riverton Spine & Rehab 34 lines at $6,290.00, medical total $15,002.40.
items.issue: The Demand Package served 07/20/2026 put the medical specials at $14,817.40. Two numbers for one file is exactly the unverified ledger Atty. Mercer named, and the difference is the 05/04/2026 duplicate.
items.fix: Rebuild the ledger line by line from the certified bills in hand: 33 attended visits × $185.00 = $6,105.00, medical $14,817.40, with wages $1,584.00 and mileage $48.79 the same $16,450.19 that was served.

items.as: Shown at $3,400.00, status "open balance", and listed to the mediator among the open balances.
items.issue: Peach State paid Crescent $1,860.00 at the contract rate and the in-network provider cannot bill the member the adjustment. Carried into the binder it concedes $3,400.00 that nobody is owed, out of John Doe's net.
items.fix: Show the charge satisfied by the plan's contract payment, proved by Peach State's EOB and the corrected $0.00 statement; the open claims are Peach State $1,860.00 and Riverton Spine & Rehab $6,105.00 = $7,965.00.

items.what: Riverton Spine & Rehab's Final Itemized Ledger
items.as: Not in hand. The line is carried at the billed figure with nothing said about it.
items.issue: An unqualified figure for a record we do not yet hold is how a ledger becomes unverifiable a second time. The chase is the Case Manager's; going further than a second request is not.
items.fix: Mark the line "Pending Final Verification", keep chasing the certified ledger, and put the subpoena question to Atty. Thorne with the request history.

items.as: The signed original of 06/30/2026, with the medical ledger and the Causation Letter.
items.issue: It proves the $1,584.00 wage claim and, separately, that John Doe was calling out of work with neck pain before he ever saw a provider.
items.fix: Confirm the 02/09–02/13/2026 call-out record stays attached to it, so the wage proof and the gap corroboration are read together.

items.as: Nowhere in the binder, though the filed Complaint pleads its counts.
items.issue: A pleaded count the mediator never sees. And once it is added, it has to sit apart: Loss of Use and Diminished Value are not John Doe's bodily injury specials and must never drift into that ledger.
items.fix: Add it as its own schedule, marked as Margaret Doe's claim and outside the $40,000 stack: Loss of Use 48 days × $42.00 = $2,016.00, Diminished Value $3,600.00 against Keystone's $792.00.

items.as: The demand of 07/20/2026 through the suit filed 09/24/2026, with each offer and its date.
items.issue: Without it nobody in the room is sure of Keystone's last number. With it, every attempt and every silence is dated.
items.fix: Confirm it sits with Keystone's own offer letter of 08/05/2026, so the number and the reasons for it are read together.

items.what: The draft release and the UM consent requests
items.as: Neither is in Section 6.
items.issue: If the file settles on the day there is nothing to sign, and no consent on its way to Harbor Point or Cardinal State, so the money stops anyway.
items.fix: Add the draft Limited Release of Robert Smith and Keystone only, and the drafted consent requests to both UM carriers. Atty. Thorne settles every term in them.

items.as: Read off the Scheduling Order as 03/31/2027.
items.issue: 03/31/2027 is the court's deadline for the mediation to be completed, not the session date. The session is 03/18/2027 and the mediator's confirmation requires the statement and binder seven days before, so 03/31 is twenty days too late.
items.fix: Docket delivery for 03/11/2027 with the approval step ahead of it, and keep 03/31/2027 on the calendar as the court's completion deadline.

d4m3-a1.revealNote: The Mediation Binder as Atty. Thorne approved it on 03/10/2027 and the firm delivered it on 03/11/2027: six sections, 141 pages, with the defense map and the rebuilt ledger. The arbitration exhibits and Day 5 both start from it.
revealPoints: Medical specials rebuilt to $14,817.40, with wages and mileage the $16,450.19 that was served on 07/20/2026.
Open liens $7,965.00: Peach State $1,860.00 and Riverton Spine & Rehab $6,105.00; Crescent $0.00.
Riverton Spine & Rehab marked "Pending Final Verification" until its certified ledger arrives.
All five pleaded allegations mapped to answering exhibits; two legal questions flagged, not answered.
Section 2 approved, marked for the mediator only, one copy; the deposition summary added at Section 4.
Delivered 03/11/2027, seven days before the 03/18/2027 session; 03/31/2027 kept as the court's deadline.

d4m3-a2.title: Sorting & QC Audit — the arbitration exhibit index
d4m3-a2.kicker: Apply each tab's QC rule before the 06/02/2027 exchange.
d4m3-a2.intro: The Litigation Desk's index of 05/14/2027. Keystone tendered at the 03/18/2027 mediation and Robert Smith was dismissed; Harbor Point and Cardinal State now dispute damages and sit on the other side of this hearing. Work it exhibit by exhibit.

items.what: Snapshot sheet and the arbitrator's fee disclosure
items.as: Tab 1: the parties, the arbitrator and the hearing date, with the fee disclosure.
items.issue: The sheet the hearing is run from. The fee disclosure belongs with it, and both carriers' claim numbers and contacts are on it.
items.fix: Confirm each carrier's contact against the file and date the check, and hold a slot for the final brief, never a draft.

items.as: Tab 1, "for background", inside the exchange set.
items.issue: It was delivered to the mediator alone and marked for the mediator only, and it is about the very carriers that are now the opposing parties. Exchanging it hands Harbor Point and Cardinal State our position in our own words.
items.fix: Withhold it from the exchange set and record why. A document marked for the mediator does not travel to the next forum.

items.as: Tab 2, the superseded draft together with the served answer.
items.issue: The draft is unsigned, carries no case number and omits pleaded counts. And the tort pleadings belong to a case that has been dismissed as to Robert Smith: whether they are exchanged here at all is not the Case Manager's call.
items.fix: Take the draft out of the file set, move the filed pleadings to the attorney's set, and put the exchange question to Atty. Thorne.

items.as: Not in the binder: no Keystone tender, no UM consents, no Limited Release, no order dismissing Robert Smith.
items.issue: UM opens only once the bodily injury layer is exhausted. Without that record the arbitrator has no reason to reach the damages tabs at all, and both carriers can say so on the first morning.
items.fix: Add them as the first exhibits of Tab 1, with both Coverage Letters: Keystone's 08/12/2026 tender, the UM consents of 08/24 and 08/26/2026, the Limited Release and the dismissal.

items.as: Tab 3, the public-redacted portal copy.
items.issue: The redactions remove the independent witness and the citation — the two things the report is in the set to prove. Offered this way it proves almost nothing.
items.fix: Order the certified complete report, redact only what this forum requires, and flag the citation's admissibility to Atty. Thorne rather than arguing it.

items.as: Tab 3, grayscale photocopies.
items.issue: Third forum, same grayscale stills. These carriers dispute damages rather than liability, but the mechanism is what makes the injury credible, and a photocopy does not show it.
items.fix: Re-export in color from the native file, hash unchanged, and log the chain of custody with the exhibit.

items.as: Tab 4, with the records and bills, at the audited figure.
items.issue: This is the figure the Demand Package served and the Mediation Binder was rebuilt to: 33 attended visits, the 05/04/2026 duplicate out. It ties.
items.fix: Confirm every line still ties to the bill behind it, and that Riverton Spine & Rehab's certified Final Itemized Ledger is the copy in the set.

items.as: None requested from any provider or record-holder.
items.issue: An uncertified record is a record a carrier can object to, and the whole ledger rests on them. Nineteen days before the exchange, nothing has been asked for.
items.fix: Request a certification from every provider and from Riverton Fire, Riverton PD and Northgate HR, and log each receipt. Nothing back in 14 days means a second request and a subpoena flag for Atty. Thorne.

items.what: MRI report and the Causation Letter
items.as: Tab 5, Dr. Park's read of 03/13/2026 and Dr. Reyes's letter of 06/19/2026.
items.issue: Together they answer the gap and the "degenerative" reading. Neither says anything about the 2021 low-back visits, which is the line defence counsel pressed at the 02/18/2027 deposition.
items.fix: Pair them with the 2021 records and the deposition testimony, and flag to Atty. Thorne whether to seek a supplemental declaration from Dr. Reyes. That is his decision, not the Case Manager's.

items.as: Not in the binder at all.
items.issue: The prior-injury line is answered by what the 2021 records actually say — three visits, low back only, resolved, no cervical complaint. Asserting it without them leaves the carriers' version standing.
items.fix: Add them at Tab 5 with the treating providers' own histories, so the damaging record and the record that answers it are read together.

items.what: Northgate wage letter and the impasse memorandum
items.as: Tab 6, the employer's letter filed together with the internal memo to Atty. Thorne.
items.issue: The memo is work product and a record of settlement communications. Filed because it explains the history, it puts our strategy and every number we discussed in front of the carriers.
items.fix: Pull the memo to the attorney's set for Atty. Thorne's privilege decision and leave Tab 6 to the wage and mileage proof alone. Nothing is exchanged, and nothing withheld, on the Case Manager's own decision.

items.what: The wage and mileage proof itself
items.as: Northgate's signed letter of 06/30/2026, and John Doe's Medical Mileage Log of 06/30/2026.
items.issue: Nine shifts × 8 hours × $22.00 = $1,584.00, proved by the employer, and 238 miles to care × $0.205 = $48.79, proved by the client's log. Tab 6 takes economic-loss proof and nothing else.
items.fix: Leave both at Tab 6 on their own, with the 02/09–02/13/2026 call-out record attached to the wage letter.

items.as: Listed as a lien because PIP paid $5,000.00 of the bills.
items.issue: Riverton's add-on PIP carries no reimbursement from the recovery, as Harbor Point's own letter of 03/02/2026 confirms, and Harbor Point is the carrier on the other side of this hearing. Working John Doe's net from a lien it does not hold costs him $5,000.00.
items.fix: Strike it, citing the 03/02/2026 letter in the threshold record. PIP paying a bill does not create a lien.

items.what: Lien Sheet — Peach State and Riverton Spine & Rehab
items.as: Peach State $1,860.00 and Riverton Spine & Rehab $6,105.00.
items.issue: Both are right: the plan's itemized reimbursement claim, and the LOP account at the audited 33 visits. Together they are the $7,965.00 the net is actually worked from.
items.fix: Confirm Crescent and Summit Imaging are shown at $0.00 as well, and reconcile the sheet to $7,965.00 before it goes to Atty. Thorne.

items.as: Not started. No exhibit records how it would be authenticated.
items.issue: A record with no logged foundation is one the carriers can object to before it is read, and at a hearing that is the same as not having it.
items.fix: Complete the column for every exhibit before the 06/02/2027 exchange, with the forum's evidence rule noted as a question for Atty. Thorne.

items.as: Docketed 06/12/2027, ten days before the hearing.
items.issue: Ten days before the hearing lands on a Saturday. A brief diaried for a day the forum is not open is a brief filed late, in the one filing that frames the whole hearing.
items.fix: Count backward and docket the earlier business day, 06/11/2027, as configured for this training file; confirm the forum's rules with Atty. Thorne.

items.as: 06/02/2027, twenty days before the hearing, as the notice sets it.
items.issue: This one is right, and it is the date every fix above has to be finished by. Everything in the set is approved before it, or it is not exchanged.
items.fix: Keep it, and work backward from it: the certifications, the colour stills and the certified report all have to land before it.

d4m3-a2.revealNote: The Arbitration Binder as Atty. Thorne approved it on 05/29/2027 and the firm exchanged it on 06/02/2027: six tabs, exhibits C-1 to C-19, 175 pages, with the withheld-items list and the audited Lien Sheet.
revealPoints: Threshold exhibits lead: the BI tender, both UM consents, the Limited Release and the dismissal.
Every record certified and authenticated; Crescent's certification chased with a subpoena flag.
Tab 5 pairs the 2021 low-back records and the deposition testimony with the MRI read and the Causation Letter.
Lien Sheet audited from $12,965.00 to $7,965.00: PIP, Summit and Crescent all at $0.00.
Six items withheld on Atty. Thorne's recorded decision, each with its reason on the file.
